question.value: Do gas scaling relations derived from star-forming galaxies extend to passive galaxies at z~0.7, and what are their molecular gas contents and kinematics?

evidence.quote: The main focus of our work here is to determine whether the scaling relations derived from observations of star-forming galaxies and cosmological simulations can accurately predict or be extrapolated down to passive galaxies at intermediate redshift.
ALMA observations of our sample of 8 galaxies were carried out in project 2016.1.00790.S (PI: Spilker)
using the Band 4 (2 mm) receivers (cite: asayama14)

method.value: Select LEGA-C galaxies at z<0.84 with log Mstar>10.8, SFR 3-10x below star-forming sequence, SFR>2.5 Msun/yr; 8 of 65 observed

evidence.quote: This resulted in a sample of 65 galaxies, from which we selected 8 for observation with ALMA

method.value: Naturally weighted continuum images and cubes; integrated spectra from point-source fits to visibilities, averaging 6 or 12 channels

evidence.quote: We extract integrated spectra for all targets by fitting point source models to the visibility data directly, averaging 6 or 12 channels

analysis_steps.goal: Measure CO fluxes and upper limits

method.value: Fit one or two Gaussians to line profiles; 3 sigma upper limits from noise in 800 km/s wide channels

evidence.quote: Integrated line fluxes are determined by fitting either one or two Gaussian profiles
we estimate upper limits on the CO emission by determining the noise in channels 800 $\rm{km\,s}^{-1}$ wide

fitting.value: Gaussian profile fits; no sampler stated

evidence.quote: Integrated line fluxes are determined by fitting either one or two Gaussian profiles, also shown in Figure [4](#fig:spectra).

method.value: Convert CO luminosity with r21 and alpha_CO; M_H2 scales as (0.8/r21)(alpha_CO/4.4)

evidence.quote: molecular gas masses can be rescaled under different assumptions as $\ensuremath{M_{\rm{H}_2}}(0.8/r_{21})(\ensuremath{\alpha_{\rm{CO}}}/4.4)$
In this work, we assume $r_{21}=0.8$.

assumptions.value: Milky Way-like alpha_CO ~50% systematic uncertainty; flat LCDM Om=0.307, H0=67.7

evidence.quote: it does still carry significant systematic uncertainty, likely of order 50%

validation.value: Cross-checked with dust-based gas mass from continuum stack

evidence.quote: This independent check indicates that our assumptions about $\alpha_{\rm{CO}}$ are reasonable.

method.value: Average image-plane inverted images/cubes of targets (continuum and CO at known redshifts)

evidence.quote: we opt to simply average together inverted images of the targets rather than perform this analysis in the Fourier plane

key_parameters.value: Dust-based M_H2: kappa_235GHz=0.42 cm2/g, Tdust=25 K, GDR=100

evidence.quote: a dust temperature $\ensuremath{T_{\rm{dust}}}= 25$ K, and a gas-to-dust ratio typical of solar metallicity systems, $\ensuremath{\delta_{\rm{GDR}}}= 100$

validation.value: Recovered sample-average line flux by stacking only CO-detected sources

evidence.quote: We have also verified that this procedure accurately recovers the sample-average line flux by stacking only the sources individually detected in CO.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare kinematics of CO and stars

method.value: Image red and blue velocity channels, fit point sources in visibility and image domain, project gradient onto N-S slit and compare with LEGA-C stellar rotation curves

evidence.quote: We fit the red and blue channels of each source in both the visibility and image domains with point source models

validation.value: Verified gradients with narrower velocity channels

evidence.quote: we have verified that the velocity gradients apparent in Figure [6](#fig:chanmaps) are consistent with imaging the data in narrower velocity channels

analysis_steps.goal: Compare with scaling relations and EAGLE

method.value: Compare f_H2 and t_dep with Scoville+17 and Tacconi+18 relations and EAGLE galaxies

evidence.quote: we compare the gas fractions and depletion times for our observed sample with two empirical scaling relations from the literature

method.value: Gas fraction declines from z=0.7 to 0 with constant t_dep and 30% mass return

evidence.quote: we construct a closed-box toy model, in which a galaxy at $z=0.75$ with $\log \ensuremath{M_{\rm{star}}}/\ensuremath{\rm{M}_\odot}=11$ continues to deplete its reservoir of molecular gas
$\ensuremath{t_{\rm{dep}}}=0.7-1.3$ Gyr, that remain constant over time

validation.value: Compared to ATLAS3D and MASSIVE local quiescent galaxies

evidence.quote: we compare to nearby quiescent galaxies with $\log \ensuremath{M_{\rm{star}}}/\ensuremath{\rm{M}_\odot}> 10.7$ selected from the ATLAS$^{\mathrm{3D}}$ and MASSIVE surveys
We clearly detect four of the eight targets in CO(2–1) emission.
a faint source with $\ensuremath{S_\mathrm{2mm}}= 17 \pm 5$ $\mu\rm{Jy}$ is detected
The CO-detected sources are detected in the 2 mm continuum stack with $\ensuremath{S_\mathrm{2mm}}= 23 \pm 7$ $\mu\rm{Jy}$
we find an average molecular gas mass for the CO-detected sources of $8.8 \times 10^9$ $\rm{M}_\odot$

results_numeric.quantity: CO stack of non-detections L'CO(2-1) upper limit (3 sigma)

evidence.quote: $\ensuremath{\rm{L}_{\rm{CO(2-1)}}'}< 5.8 \times 10^8$ K $\rm{km\,s}^{-1}$ pc$^2$
this is equivalent to $\ensuremath{M_{\rm{H}_2}}< 3.2 \times 10^9$ $\rm{M}_\odot$
the resulting upper limit on the gas fraction of these passive sources is $\ensuremath{f_{\rm{H}_2}}=\ensuremath{M_{\rm{H}_2}}/\ensuremath{M_{\rm{star}}}<0.016$

results_numeric.quantity: CO centroid precision of red/blue components

evidence.quote: the centroids of each velocity component can be determined to $\approx$0.3$''$, on average

findings_qualitative.value: Detected galaxies have M_H2 ≲1e10 Msun, over an order of magnitude above local early types, with depletion times ≲1-2 Gyr.

evidence.quote: the $\lesssim$1–2 Gyr depletion times are typical of, or even shorter than, galaxies near the star-forming sequence.

findings_qualitative.value: CO and stellar rotation axes are consistent in at least three of four detections.

evidence.quote: the rotational axes of the stellar and molecular components of the CO-detected objects are consistent in at least three of four cases.

claims.hypothesis: Gas scaling relations from star-forming galaxies extrapolate to passive galaxies at z~0.7
claims.experiment: Compare f_H2 and t_dep with Scoville+17 and Tacconi+18 relations
claims.result: Relations over-predict f_H2 and t_dep, especially for non-detections (stack f_gas factor 5 lower, t_dep factor 4)
claims.finding: Break or increased scatter in scaling relations at low sSFR

evidence.quote: It is apparent that the literature scaling relations cannot be extrapolated and lose predictive power at the low sSFRs probed by our sample.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas was accreted externally after quenching
claims.experiment: Compare CO velocity gradients with LEGA-C stellar rotation
claims.finding: Gas not likely accreted after quenching

evidence.quote: This argues against an external origin for the molecular gas in $z\sim0.7$ passive galaxies

claims.hypothesis: These galaxies evolve into local massive early types without further gas accretion
claims.experiment: Closed-box toy model with low-level star formation
claims.result: Reproduces range of f_H2 in nearby passive galaxies
claims.finding: No need for extra accretion or dynamical stabilization

evidence.quote: can very naturally reproduce the range of $f_{\rm{H}_2}$ seen in nearby passive galaxies, with no need for further gas accretion or dramatic increase in $t_{\rm{dep}}$.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting maximizes sensitivity to faint emission

evidence.quote: which maximizes sensitivity to faint emission in exchange for slightly lower spatial resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample of 8; alpha_CO systematic uncertainty ~50%; SFR from 24um may be overestimated up to ~2x

evidence.quote: With only 8 target galaxies in total, we cannot draw strong conclusions on this point.
